title: Marine Fighter Pilot Saw a 737-Sized Object Hovering Over Houston — ATC Tracked It | Ben Read
description:
A former Marine F-18 Hornet pilot with 18 years of service describes the encounter that turned him from skeptic to witness: a wingless, mercury-like object "the size of a 737" hovering motionless in his climb path out of Houston — while air traffic control reported an uncorrelated target that had been popping on and off radar all day. At roughly 500 feet, it accelerated away faster than anything he'd seen in two decades of military and commercial flying.

Former Navy F/A-18F pilot Ryan Graves (Americans for Safe Aerospace) talks with Benjamin Read about his path from enlisted helicopter mechanic to single-seat Hornet pilot, a career-threatening spinal injury during an air show for the Thai Royal Family, recovering fallen Americans in Iraq with Task Force Personnel Recovery, why his time as a general's aide made him assume every strange light was a classified U.S. program — and why he now tells fellow pilots: "Don't be a coward."

Americans for Safe Aerospace (ASA) is a nonprofit dedicated to aviation safety, airspace transparency, and scientific investigation of unidentified anomalous phenomena, founded by Ryan Graves, the first active-duty pilot to come forward publicly about UAP and witness before Congress.
